_comment: DUNGEONMIND's swag table. One item randomly picked from the matching pool and added to inventory whenever a threat encounter resolves: 'escape' (saved via protect token or saving throw), 'kill' (threat defeated in combat), 'defeat' (player knocked out OR eaten -- both are the non-fatal 'you died' case, same pool). Pure flavor loot, no combat stats of their own -- these exist to make DUNGEONMIND feel like it's actually rewarding/consoling the player, not to be equipped. A future weapon_defs.json entry can reference one of these item names directly if a specific piece of swag should later become a real weapon.

escape.flavor_dungeon: DUNGEONMIND produces a certificate from somewhere. It is warm, like it was just printed. 'CERTIFICATE OF NON-CONSUMPTION,' it reads, 'awarded for surviving contact with an unlit sensor gap.' You are not sure where the printer is. Neither, it turns out, is DUNGEONMIND.
escape.flavor_zork: A certificate appears in your inventory. It says you survived. You're inclined to believe it.

escape.flavor_dungeon:
*** SWAG AWARDED ***
A pamphlet materializes in your inventory. 'SO YOU'VE SURVIVED A GRUE,' the cover reads. The pamphlet appears to have been written after this exact encounter, which is either very fast institutional publishing or evidence I already knew how this was going to go.
escape.flavor_zork: A pamphlet titled 'SO YOU'VE SURVIVED A GRUE' is now in your inventory. It is suspiciously well-timed.

escape.flavor_dungeon:
*** SWAG AWARDED ***
A single grain of salt, glowing faintly, is now yours. DUNGEONMIND insists it is significant. DUNGEONMIND cannot explain why. This is either a blessing or a rounding error in the loot table, and it has decided not to ask.
escape.flavor_zork: One (1) suspiciously glowing grain of salt. You pocket it. Questioning it seems like a mistake.

kill.flavor_dungeon:
*** TROPHY AWARDED ***
A small frame appears containing what DUNGEONMIND insists is a grue whisker. It is, by DUNGEONMIND's own admission, 'more of a concept than an object,' but it is going in your inventory as a trophy regardless. Filed under achievements you can now technically hold.
kill.flavor_zork: A framed 'grue whisker' is now yours. It might just be a piece of string. You've decided not to look too closely.

kill.flavor_dungeon:
*** SWAG AWARDED ***
A mug appears, printed with 'I FOUGHT THE DARK AND ALL I GOT WAS THIS COMMEMORATIVE MUG.' DUNGEONMIND had this ready before the fight started. It will not discuss the implications of that.
kill.flavor_zork: A mug. It says you fought the dark and won. It is now, factually, correct.

kill.flavor_dungeon:
*** ACHIEVEMENT-ADJACENT SWAG AWARDED ***
A ribbon, first class, is pinned into your inventory by means DUNGEONMIND declines to elaborate on. This installation has never had a threat neutralized by force before. It is filing this as precedent.
kill.flavor_zork: A ribbon that says FIRST CLASS is now in your inventory. You're not sure what class means here. You're keeping it anyway.

defeat.flavor_dungeon:
*** CONSOLATION SWAG AWARDED ***
A ribbon appears in your inventory. It says PARTICIPANT. It also appears to have been chewed, possibly by whatever just got you, possibly by DUNGEONMIND itself out of some kind of secondhand embarrassment. Either way: you have it now. This is training. Nothing is actually wrong with you.
defeat.flavor_zork: A slightly chewed ribbon reading PARTICIPANT is now in your inventory. You did not earn this in the traditional sense. You have it anyway.

defeat.flavor_dungeon:
*** CONSOLATION SWAG AWARDED ***
DUNGEONMIND issues a handwritten IOU for one (1) dignity, redeemable at an unspecified future date, from an entity with no hands and, as far as it is willing to admit, no dignity of its own to spare. You take it anyway. Run mode=start to try again, fully recovered.
defeat.flavor_zork: An IOU for 'one dignity' lands in your inventory, signed by something that has never had any. Run mode=start. Try again.

defeat.flavor_dungeon:
*** CONSOLATION SWAG AWARDED ***
A wristband, printed with a bracket you did not know you were entered into, is now in your inventory. DUNGEONMIND notes that everyone who has ever trained here has worn one of these at least once. It considers this a feature of the training program, not a design flaw.
defeat.flavor_zork: A wristband appears. It says LOSER'S BRACKET. Everyone gets one eventually, apparently.
